import Mathlib
import Nodes.«spec-137537c8».Context

/-- The Lambert identity for Erdős 257: for every `A ⊆ ℕ`, the sum `∑_{a ∈ A} 1/(2^a - 1)` is the
binary series `∑_{m ≥ 1} f_A(m) / 2^m` whose `m`-th coefficient `f_A(m) = #{a ∈ A : a ∣ m}` counts
the divisors of `m` that lie in `A`. It is the first line of every published irrationality
argument for this problem (Erdős 1948 with `f_ℕ = d`, Erdős 1968, Luca–Tachiya 2014,
Duverney–Tachiya 2019, Tao–Teräväinen with `f = ω`) and of the carry bookkeeping of the
greedy walk. The term at `m = 0` is `0` (the set `{a ∈ A | 0 < m ∧ a ∣ m}` is empty there), and
in Lean a `0 ∈ A` contributes `1/0 = 0` on the left and divides no `m ≥ 1` on the right, so no
hypothesis on `A` is needed. -/
theorem Opn.erdos_257_lambert_identity :
    ∀ (A : Set ℕ),
    ∑' n : A, (1 : ℝ) / (2 ^ n.1 - 1) =
      ∑' m : ℕ, (Set.ncard {a ∈ A | 0 < m ∧ a ∣ m} : ℝ) / 2 ^ m := by
  sorry

literature_proposed.summary: Open: nothing in print decides whether 1/2 (or any rational) is an infinite subset sum. If true, it refutes Erdős 257. Evidence: the greedy walk for 1/2 survives to depth 10^8 (Hong, unrefereed); the subsum set has measure 1 (Nitecki Thm 4 with Kovač–Tao Remark 4.1), so a 'random' real lies in it with probability about 0.62, but the rationals are a null set and positive measure alone decides nothing. Kovač (forum, Aug 2025) expects the base-2 set to contain dyadic rationals such as 1/2, heuristically; for bases t ≥ 3 the set is null and he expects no rationals.

import Mathlib
import Nodes.«spec-a70fcca4-v2».Context

/-- The natural counterexample candidate for Erdős 257, stated so that it can be proved or
refuted: `1/2` is the Mersenne reciprocal sum of some infinite set. A finite set cannot give
`1/2` (finite sums have odd denominators), so any representation of `1/2` is infinite, and a
proof of this statement refutes the root. The greedy walk for `1/2` (the only possible
representation) begins 2, 3, 6, 7, 14, 20, 21, 26, 27, 32, ... and has been run without stalling
to depth 2500 here and to depth 10^8 by Hong (Zenodo 23287959, 2026, unrefereed); Kovač
(erdosproblems.com/257, Aug 2025) expects the subset-sum set, a fat Cantor set, to contain
such rationals. No proof in either direction is known. -/
theorem Opn.erdos_257_half_is_a_subsum :
    ∃ A : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧ ∑' n : A, (1 : ℝ) / (2 ^ n.1 - 1) = 1 / 2 := by
  sorry
